summary: Morgan Point Light, at the mouth of the Mystic River in Noank, Connecticut, was lit in 1831 and discontinued in 1921 after a run of keepers, two of them women.

access.note: A private residence; grounds and dwelling closed to the public. Best viewed from the water.

corrections.why: The keeper retired in 1919 (Norwich Bulletin, 15 April 1919). The light itself was discontinued about two weeks before 7 September 1921 (Norwich Bulletin, 7 September 1921), and LighthouseFriends gives 1921.

No source describes a conical tower. LighthouseFriends and D'Entremont describe a granite dwelling with an octagonal or cast-iron lantern; the USLHS record lists an octagonal wooden tower on a granite dwelling.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS and Wikidata give 1919, the year keeper Pecor retired. The Norwich Bulletin of 7 September 1921 reports the light was discontinued about two weeks earlier, and LighthouseFriends gives 1921. The 1921 date is the discontinuance; 1919 is the keeper's retirement.

Wikidata gives 'conical masonry'. The USLHS record gives an octagonal wooden tower on a granite dwelling. D'Entremont and LighthouseFriends describe a granite dwelling with an octagonal or cast-iron lantern. No source says conical.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster is the USLHS list (matched by name and position, 0.76 km). Alexander and Frances McDonald's dates differ across sources: USLHS 1866-1869 and 1869-1871; LighthouseFriends 1866-1870 and 1870-1871; D'Entremont 1867-1869 and 1869-1871. USLHS dates are used. Silas Spicer is spelled Spencer once in LighthouseFriends. D'Entremont's list gives Reilly for the last keeper; USLHS and the 1921 Norwich Bulletin (OCR 'Rilty') point to Riley. The 1919 and 1921 Norwich Bulletin pages are OCR with columns running together, so the quotations were chosen from clean runs of words; the 1868 date in the 1921 article is unreadable in OCR and is cited to other sources instead. Pecor's 1871 appointment year comes from the roster; the Norwich Bulletin gives 'Secretary Boutwell' with no year. Bache's 1838 inspection report is not in the corpus; it is quoted second-hand through LighthouseFriends, and the original was not checked. D'Entremont's burning-vessel rescue (Spicer) and the frostbitten-sailors account have no dates beyond the keeper's tenure and no second source. They are included with attribution. A newspaper check for them is still open. Riley's transfer to Stuyvesant Landing is from the Norwich Bulletin only; the station named there is not checked. Private individuals are not named: the 1991 buyer, the later summer residents. D'Entremont's claim that Henry Davis supervised the 1868 construction and later became a Life-Saving official was left out (identity not established). Record values not supported by the sources read: the tower height 15.8 m (Wikidata) against USLHS 44 ft (13.4 m); focal height 18.6 m against USLHS 60 ft (18.3 m); the 'conical_masonry' type. See corrections. The 1921 discontinuance date conflicts with the 1919 date in USLHS and Wikidata; the 1919 date is the keeper's retirement (see resolved_conflicts). The 1938 hurricane account and the lantern removal remain unresolved. The record's Commons photo was not reviewed for licence. Newspaper searches: Chronicling America hits for 'Morgan Point' 1921-1923 (five hits, three read) and for Pecor with Morgan Point 1871-1918 (one hit, read; personal family detail left out). The LHB reports of 1891-1901 list Morgan Point as a station only; not used. Wikipedia was used for leads only. Verification 2026-10-28: the Frances McDonald start year is stated in the story as a disagreement (USLHS 1869, LighthouseFriends 1870). The discontinuance disagreement (USLHS 'Year Discontinued: 1919' against the 1921 Norwich Bulletin reports) is stated in the story. The 'do not land' sentence is now a plain statement of the private, closed status in the sources, not a quotation.
